call_sites: reckon/mcp.py:server import surface (read_plan, roadmap, crew, audit, edit_plan registration)

findings.text: follow-on: `_mounts_path as _mounts_path` is a redundant-alias import of a name no longer used by the module's own code; its only reader is tests/test_mcp_views.py:520 (`mcp_module._mounts_path()`). Production callers import `_mounts_path` from reckon._store directly. The alias keeps a test coupled to the server's import surface; importing `_mounts_path` from reckon._store in that test would let the alias go.

follow-on: the family-reload helper repairs the test scaffolding but the underlying hazard stays in the shipped design: a moved module (reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py) binds the store's exception class by import, so any future straight reload of reckon._store leaves its except clauses stale until it is reloaded too. The helper is the right fix for the 28 fixtures that reload, and it is shared and dependency-ordered; a one-line module docstring naming this coupling as the reason any reload must include the whole family (not just the store) would keep the next splitter from reintroducing it.

follow-on: the gate log this node cites (r-20261008T220009884737-mcp-module-split-moved/gate.log) begins with `bringing up nodes...` and never states the revision, tree or command it ran, and the final manifest's baseline_suite/after_suite fields are empty, so the added-failure claim is not machine-readable in the manifest. Adding the standard gate header (revision, tree, command) would make the evidence self-describing; the run's own whole-family reload proof already carries the equivalent facts in its tests line.

follow-on: the node's declared 26-file gate did not reach edit_plan's refusal paths, so a 57-failure whole-suite regression (all uncaught reckon._store.OpError on edit_plan refusal) was invisible to the node and was found only by the coordinator's whole-suite measure at the merged head. The gate selection is the organising defect here rather than the code: the fix landed and the repaired head is green, but a future move-touching node should include the modules that exercise the moved code's refusal paths in its gate.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base 75514321. 1745e49b2 is the move: mcp.py sheds ~3,248 lines, the three produced modules gain 919/803/1485 lines, the size-guard allowlist drops its mcp.py entry, the census tests are repointed to the module whose code now reads the patched name, and the shared-write-paths reason is rewritten. d8cda9053 adds the one-line `_mounts_path` re-export and reloads reckon.mcp_edit_plan in the store fixture. 0e6b2578 records the first landing fragment. 76ef2e3e7 adds tests/mcp_family_reload.py and points 23 reloading fixtures at it. d11f64b72 records the family-reload proof in the fragment. The diff 75514321..d11f64b72 touches 38 paths, every one inside the granted scope; the coordinator's resume-2 ruling extended the grant to the 28 reloading modules.
item_verdicts.done_when: I reproduced each clause of section 7 at the reviewed head d11f64b72. scripts/check_pure_move.py --base 75514321 --module reckon/mcp.py --into the three produced modules prints 134 moved / 76 new (all imports) / 0 problems, EXIT=0. Module sizes are reckon/mcp.py 32130 / mcp_deadlines 9913 / mcp_discovery 8241 / mcp_edit_plan 14826 estimated tokens, all under the 40000 target. tests/test_every_module_fits_a_worker_window.py passes 4/4 with reckon/mcp.py absent from ALLOWLIST, so the ratchet arm holding an under-bound listed module in red is exercised. The registered tool set (audit, crew, edit_plan, read_plan, roadmap) and their parameter schemas were byte-identical base vs head at the earlier head and are unchanged by the two later commits (fragment text and test fixtures only).
item_verdicts.goal: Section 7 asks that reckon/mcp.py, one of three modules just over the bound, be split so the module and every module it produced sit at or under 40,000 estimated tokens, with a pure move, the guard passing with mcp.py removed from its allowlist, the tool functions registered on the same server under the same names, and the gate showing no failure absent at base. The move relocates mcp.py's storage deadlines into reckon/mcp_deadlines.py, its project-discovery helpers into reckon/mcp_discovery.py and its edit_plan tool into reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py, leaving the read_plan, roadmap, crew and audit surfaces and the registration block in reckon/mcp.py. Every element is present and independently re-measured.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; the final manifest records status complete, commits 1745e49b2/d8cda9053/0e6b25783/76ef2e3e7/d11f64b72, the pure-move receipt and sizes, the tool-schema parity claim, the family-reload proof and the gate parity. Its baseline_suite/after_suite fields are empty, so the added-failure link rests on the run's own whole-suite logs (mcp-base-fail.txt, mcp-head-fail.txt) and the head gate (gate.log) rather than on a machine-readable pair; I re-derived the parity from those logs and from my own run of the affected files. mcp-head-fail.txt captures the pre-repair state (74 failures vs the base 17) and is the record of the regression the repair addressed, not of the reviewed head.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the grant lists the four reckon modules, the size-guard file, the repointed mcp tests, the census/capability/graph/rollup tests, docs/state/reckon/shared-write-paths.json and the landing fragment; the coordinator's resume-2 ruling explicitly granted the 28 reloading test modules and tests/mcp_family_reload.py, which the repair needed. The diff 75514321..d11f64b72 touches 38 paths, every one inside the (extended) grant and none outside it.

justifications.durability: the size guard is a self-cleaning ratchet that reddens both when a module grows past the bound unlisted and when a completed split leaves its entry behind (4 tests exercise both arms); the run's declared size mutation reddens (1 failed, EXIT=1 in negative-control.log) and I reproduced the guard at head. The lasting residual is the module-level binding of the store's exception class by the moved tool module: the family-reload helper repairs the fixtures, but the coupling itself is not guarded, so a future split that moves a caught exception can reintroduce the staleness. Below 20 for that, and for the `_mounts_path` alias kept only for a test attribute read.
justifications.evidence: I reproduced the pure-move receipt (0 problems, EXIT=0), the four module sizes, the size guard (4 passed) and the repair of the whole-suite regression: running the 13 files that mcp-head-fail.txt names but mcp-base-fail.txt does not, at head d11f64b72, gives 187 passed, EXIT=0, so the 57 added failures the run's own logs recorded are repaired at the reviewed head. The residual weakness is that gate.log carries no header naming its revision, tree and command, and the final manifest's baseline_suite/after_suite are empty, so the added-failure claim is not machine-readable in the manifest itself (the run's tests line carries the family-reload proof instead).
justifications.fit: the split follows the section-8 contract: every moved statement is carried byte-identical into exactly one module, patches are repointed to the module whose code now reads them, and the server re-exports the moved names so the import surface is unchanged. The repair is correctly scoped to tests (the moved bodies are unchanged), and the shared helper fixes the whole family in one place rather than per-fixture.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/mcp.py is split into three cohesive sibling modules and stands at 32130 estimated tokens; the produced modules are 9913 / 8241 / 14826; the tool functions stay registered under the same names with identical schemas; section 7's deliverable is met in full. Not 20 because the delivered split crossed the store-exception identity in a way the node's own gate could not observe, requiring a mid-flight repair.
justifications.reuse: the token estimate is taken from reckon.crew.routing._tokens_for_bytes rather than a second copy of the ratio, the move is checked by the shared scripts/check_pure_move.py, the reload repair is one shared helper rather than 23 copies, and no moved code is re-derived.
